objective: Package 173B registers only the finite portable immutable same-origin production web/API image and serialized migration-before-rollout gate. This PR changes governance only; a separate post-merge implementation may change the exact 13 listed paths.
requirements: Haseeb explicitly accepted the APBRA-173B architecture and controller refinements in Jira 10522 in his 2026-10-05 instruction, including a 45-minute APBRA Bootstrap job ceiling. Owner decision 10471 still makes Azure Container Apps/Job a reference deployment profile, not core product logic. This acceptance does not select region, SKU, spend, networking, preview URL, live Entra, paid provider or recovery targets.

Create one portable immutable same-origin web/API image. The build must compile the existing React/Vite application into exact versioned static bytes and package those bytes with FastAPI and existing Node bridges. Vite development/preview proxy and legacy Azure AI proxy are never the hosted production runtime. No new frontend framework, dependency or lockfile change is authorised.

Pin public static routing to GET and HEAD / and /invite returning the built shell, plus manifest-reachable, hashed asset files under /assets/. There is no general SPA fallback, directory listing, source-map exposure by default, arbitrary file serving or public path to evidence, reference material, generated artifacts, secrets or local test fixtures. Private content continues through current protected API/database authority.

The built index/shell must revalidate rather than use immutable caching. Manifest-reachable hashed assets may use immutable long-lived caching; unknown assets fail 404. The exact built asset closure must be checked so stale or missing manifest references fail rather than being silently served. No stale index may point at missing assets after rollout/rollback.

All /api routes remain FastAPI routes. Unknown API paths and methods retain API 404/405 semantics and never receive the SPA. /dev/oidc, /docs, /openapi.json and every other non-app route keep their existing explicit behavior or 404; this package grants no authentication or API contract change.

The repository-root Docker build context requires an effective Dockerfile-specific apps/api/Dockerfile.dockerignore. Exclude .env and secret-bearing local files, private content roots, artifacts, caches, Git metadata, development build output and unrelated workspace material from transferred context. Verify actual context exclusion with synthetic marker files; do not assume apps/api/.dockerignore applies to a root context.

For hosted release, run one explicit Alembic migration step before app rollout; do not run migration or local bootstrap on every hosted replica start. Serialize the entire online migration using a PostgreSQL advisory lock held by the same connection executing migrations, with bounded lock/startup waits and deterministic release/connection cleanup. Failure or timeout blocks rollout. No cloud runner/IaC is implemented in 173B.

Rollback is image-based only after explicit schema compatibility verification between the previous image and migrated schema. Never automatically downgrade a production schema, treat successful app restart as migration proof, or roll out a new image after failed migration. Preserve existing local Compose development behavior unless separately governed.

Mandatory CI must build and start the actual image and test public shell/assets, API health and unknown-API 404, no replica startup migration/bootstrap, private/static separation and effective context exclusions using synthetic markers. Every failing or timed-out smoke step fails CI, and cleanup is bounded and reliable.

The APBRA Bootstrap job keeps its required runner, read-only permissions and mandatory checks; future implementation may add the image smoke and change only the exact job timeout from 30 to 45 minutes through the registered workflow, CI policy checker, bootstrap checker and CI policy test paths. The ceiling is a validation budget, not measured speed improvement or permission for skipped tests.

Registration changes exactly five governance files. The APBRA-177 historical source-position test may change only its tail-dependent location/mutation assertions to stable contiguous ID-based assertions; all historical source rows, hashes, task contracts and gates stay unchanged. Future implementation changes only the exact 13 unique literal allowed_paths after exact-head CI, separate independent review, Haseeb manual registration merge and verified main.

PostgreSQL online migrations require a single same-connection serialization point and bounded failure behavior; schema compatibility determines image rollback eligibility. No application replica performs opportunistic migration.

APBRA-173C durable requirement-analysis, automatic-design and candidate-generation work remains separately governed, with shared PostgreSQL claim/lease/fencing and distinct retry, cancellation, revocation and publication gates.

acceptance_criteria: The registration PR changes exactly five governance paths and no product, Docker, workflow or runtime file. Future implementation has exactly 13 literal paths, no glob, no fourteenth path, no migration revision and no new dependency.

Actual built image serves GET/HEAD / and /invite as a revalidating shell and only manifest-reachable hashed /assets files with immutable caching; missing/stale/unknown assets, unknown application routes and path traversal fail 404. API unknown routes return API 404 rather than index HTML; API methods retain their semantics.

Private evidence, reference material, generated artifacts, secret files, source files, test fixtures and build-context marker files are absent from the static root and final image, and no private object can be downloaded through a public path.

A Dockerfile-specific ignore for the effective root context excludes synthetic secret/private markers before build transfer, while every required source/lockfile is still available to build. Image build is reproducible from the exact checkout without Vite hosted runtime or browser-visible credentials.

Two concurrent online migration processes serialize on one same-connection PostgreSQL lock for the entire migration. Bounded lock timeout and process failure clean up; a failed or timed-out migration blocks rollout. Hosted app start is migration/bootstrap-free. Previous-image rollback is allowed only after compatibility verification; no automatic schema downgrade.

Actual image build/start smoke covers shell, asset closure, cache headers, API health and 404, private/static separation, excluded markers, no startup migration/bootstrap, failure propagation and bounded cleanup. Its timeout/crash is not PASS.

The future workflow retains every mandatory check, uses the same read-only runner permissions, adds mandatory image smoke and pins a 45-minute job ceiling with matching CI-policy and bootstrap-policy checks; no paid runner, skipped suite or ignored exit status.

Historical APBRA-177 accepted source IDs, order, hashes and source rows stay intact; only source-position assertion logic is repaired so later append-only rows are allowed while historical reordering/mutation remains rejected.

No Azure deployment, 173C worker, live Entra, hosted durability/recovery, Power BI Desktop, production readiness, Live Canvas/ARD, billing or connected publishing claim follows from registration or deterministic image smoke.
